labs.title: Record a bench inventory
labs.goal: Separate host/tool evidence from an assumed board identity.
labs.inputs: Python 3.12; no attached device required.
steps: Run the read-only inventory.
Inspect the serial candidates, if any.
Write the actual board identification as unknown until verified separately.
labs.expected: JSON identifies the Python/platform and candidate paths; devices_opened is false. An empty candidate list is a valid observation.
labs.failures: A path is not a model. A USB data cable, boot mode, OS permission or absent device can explain no candidates.

labs.title: Verify firmware bytes
labs.goal: Match an artifact to a separately recorded expected SHA-256.
labs.inputs: The synthetic example manifest and text fixture; neither is firmware.
steps: Read the fixture manifest and identify its expected digest.
Run the helper with that exact digest.
Change one digest character and confirm refusal.
labs.expected: A correct digest returns verified=true and the byte count. The altered digest returns exit 1.
labs.failures: Do not replace an expected digest with the observed value after a mismatch; a hash match alone does not authenticate a publisher.

labs.title: Refuse an invalid flash plan
labs.goal: Demonstrate that metadata and example-only checks occur before any hardware action.
labs.inputs: Example-only manifest; a port string is an explicit plan input, not an opened device.
steps: Read board/chip/kind/offset fields.
Run the example-only plan request.
Inspect the rejection and confirm that no command was executed.
labs.expected: Exit 1 explains that the example fixture cannot produce a board-write plan.
labs.failures: An app-only/OTA image, wrong board or wrong chip must not be silently accepted. Real plans remain dry runs.

labs.title: Inspect a UF2 structure
labs.goal: Distinguish a valid block structure from authenticated, board-compatible firmware.
labs.inputs: A UF2 obtained from an official source, or the synthetic block constructed by the parser tests.
steps: Check whole 512-byte blocks.
Inspect magic values and complete sequence.
Keep structural validity separate from family compatibility and signatures.
labs.expected: Tests accept a deliberately constructed complete block and reject corrupted/truncated sequences.
labs.failures: No UF2 from this exercise is reported as flashed or bootable; do not write synthetic parser fixtures to hardware.

labs.title: Find pin-map conflicts
labs.goal: Separate a legitimate shared signal from conflicting functions assigned to one pin.
labs.inputs: Two authored JSON net fixtures.
steps: Run the shared-clock fixture.
Run the conflicting chip-select fixture.
Explain which checks still require a schematic and electrical review.
labs.expected: First fixture succeeds with three unique pins; second fails on pin 5.
labs.failures: Equal net names do not validate voltage, current, timing or bus arbitration.

labs.title: Read a local HTTP response
labs.goal: Distinguish HTTP 200, HTTP 404 and a transport failure.
labs.inputs: Python local server and the harmless health fixture.
steps: Start the loopback fixture server.
Request health.json and a missing path.
Stop your server and repeat to observe a connection error.
labs.expected: The full guide supplies second-terminal requests. Expect 200/404 while running, then connection failure after stopping.
labs.failures: Do not claim a 404 is a connection failure. The helper rejects external targets and redirects.

labs.title: Decode a fictional BLE advertisement
labs.goal: Inspect length/type/value fields without inferring a device identity.
labs.inputs: Hex bytes containing Flags and the fictional local name LAB1.
steps: Decode the supplied bytes.
Identify the length, type and payload separately.
Run the truncated example and retain its error.
labs.expected: The first yields two fields including LAB1; the second fails as truncated.
labs.failures: A local name can be chosen by a device. No camera, operator or vendor identity follows from this decode.

labs.title: Measure message delivery
labs.goal: Keep missing observations separate from observed latency.
labs.inputs: Ten fictional message rows, with synchronized fixture timestamps.
steps: Count sent and observed rows.
Compute delivery and latency for observed rows only.
Explain what missing data and clock disagreement would change.
labs.expected: 10 sent, 8 observed, 2 missing, delivery fraction 0.8, median latency 60 ms.
labs.failures: No radio range or product comparison follows from this synthetic dataset. Duplicate sequences and receive-before-send inputs fail.

labs.title: Calculate an energy budget
labs.goal: Turn explicit duty/current assumptions into a planning estimate.
labs.inputs: Battery-side active/idle currents at one consistent voltage.
steps: Write the assumed workload fractions.
Run the weighted-current calculation.
Vary one assumption and record the sensitivity.
labs.expected: 12.5 mA average and 76.8 estimated hours using 80% usable capacity.
labs.failures: This excludes aging, temperature and nonlinear discharge. It is not a measured runtime claim for a named node.

labs.title: Build an exact ESP32 target
labs.goal: Match MCU, display, keyboard, partitions and peripherals to a supported build.
labs.inputs: An owned board and its exact current manual/release.
steps: Inventory the complete target.
Build using the project-pinned SDK/environment.
Follow the official install/recovery route and test one desired function.
labs.expected: Record a real build result, installed version and functional observation. Hardware execution is not claimed by this repository.
labs.failures: A matching chip alone does not establish matching carrier pins or a valid artifact layout.

labs.title: Write a Flipper external app
labs.goal: Build a harmless logging application and understand FAP API/RAM constraints.
labs.inputs: Pinned official firmware SDK and examples/flipper_hello.
steps: Copy the authored app into applications_user.
Build with fbt using the exact SDK.
On an owned device, follow the official launch path and inspect the startup log.
labs.expected: A FAP build and actual log are separate evidence. The example has not been physically run here.
labs.failures: External app code consumes RAM and requires compatible API metadata; a filename is insufficient.

labs.title: Set up a role-specific mesh node
labs.goal: Choose tracker, keyboard node, solar node or PoE gateway by its actual role.
labs.inputs: Owned model-specific node(s), correct regional RF hardware and current target image.
steps: Record role and exact board.
Set the documented region/firmware target.
Run a controlled stationary baseline before changing placement.
labs.expected: Retain model/configuration, delivery counts, missing messages and power conditions.
labs.failures: M1/M5, V4/V4-R8 and OLED/e-paper targets are not interchangeable.

labs.title: Build an owned RFID fixture
labs.goal: Separate model capability, implemented mode and repeated observation.
labs.inputs: Owned reference reader/tags and a supported PM3/Chameleon setup.
steps: Choose reader versus emulator role.
Record client/firmware and mode support.
Repeat a bounded identification/response fixture and retain negative cases.
labs.expected: A versioned compatibility record and reference-fixture observations, not a general access-control conclusion.
labs.failures: Proxmark5 maturity and Chameleon Lite reader limitations are documented separately.

labs.title: Budget an SDR receive path
labs.goal: Record sample/gain settings and a safe input-level budget before interpreting data.
labs.inputs: Owned SDR and a known controlled reference input.
steps: Identify half/full duplex and conversion resolution.
Calculate the input path and attenuation from the exact manual.
Record a short receive-only baseline and inspect clipping.
labs.expected: Keep raw samples, settings, input assumptions and negative cases.
labs.failures: An uncalibrated spectrum display is not a calibrated power measurement or a device identity.

labs.title: Recover a Linux handheld
labs.goal: Prove a complete carrier/image/peripheral combination and a separate recovery medium.
labs.inputs: Exact owned compute module/carrier, official image and known-good removable medium.
steps: Record the whole machine.
Verify the image and explicitly identify target storage.
Boot, test the needed peripherals, then boot the independent recovery medium.
labs.expected: Record image/kernel, keyboard/display/storage checks and a real restoration observation.
labs.failures: No guessed disk-write command is supplied. A shared enclosure does not imply a shared image.

labs.title: Write a harmless YARA rule
labs.goal: Explain a match using authored marker text and a negative fixture.
labs.inputs: YARA CLI plus the original training rule/text.
steps: Read the file-size and marker conditions.
Run the positive text fixture and negative health JSON.
Change the fixture and explain the result without assigning malware identity.
labs.expected: Only the authored training text should match. Requires the optional YARA CLI.
labs.failures: A rule match proves its condition, not malware attribution; this is not a real malware dataset.

labs.title: Inspect a binary you wrote
labs.goal: Connect source, compiled behavior and decompiler reconstruction.
labs.inputs: C compiler; optional Ghidra; examples/benign_counter.c.
steps: Build a debug version into /tmp.
Run it and record output.
Inspect main/loop in Ghidra and compare an optimized build.
labs.expected: The executable prints observed=3. Ghidra interaction is an optional manual exercise.
labs.failures: Do not download unknown executables or call decompiled text the original source.

labs.title: Cross-check a cryptographic digest
labs.goal: Compare two implementations on the same harmless bytes.
labs.inputs: OpenSSL CLI and the authored text fixture.
steps: Calculate SHA-256 with OpenSSL.
Compare with the manifest and Python helper.
Change a copy and explain the mismatch.
labs.expected: The digest matches the fixture manifest exactly; changed bytes do not.
labs.failures: Integrity and source authentication are different claims.

labs.title: Observe a local web application passively
labs.goal: Pair a request/response with a passive finding without generating attack traffic.
labs.inputs: Owned local fixture and disposable browser profile; optional Burp or ZAP.
steps: Start the fixture.
Observe one request with active actions disabled.
Trace any passive alert to the exact message/rule and discuss false positives.
labs.expected: A bounded local request/response record; no scanner/exploitation result is claimed.
labs.failures: Interception, passive history and active scanning are different actions. Avoid unrelated personal sessions.

labs.title: Read protocol evidence offline
labs.goal: Trace a decoded field back to stored bytes and capture context.
labs.inputs: TShark/Wireshark and a harmless saved capture you own.
steps: Record capture provenance.
Identify the packet bytes for one decoded field.
Compare a display filter with the original packet population.
labs.expected: A source/field/byte explanation and explicit observation limits.
labs.failures: A filter cannot recover traffic missing from the capture; encrypted payloads remain unavailable without authorized keys.

labs.title: Model an update state machine
labs.goal: Define transitions that exclude unverified or mismatched artifacts.
labs.inputs: Paper/state diagram and the helper validation tests.
steps: Define known_good/downloaded/verified/staged/booted/recovered states.
Write invariants for staging and recovery.
Use parser/manifest negative cases as examples, not a proof of the whole bootloader.
labs.expected: The software invariants are exercised; the physical bootloader remains a separate system.
labs.failures: A finite test suite is not exhaustive formal verification.

labs.title: Review hardware/software provenance
labs.goal: Distinguish physical revision, firmware artifact and source-document identity.
labs.inputs: One reviewed product page and its primary-source receipt.
steps: Read a source-linked feature.
Record document URL/retrieval/digest and whether it is manufacturer or maintainer evidence.
Distinguish a stated rating, roadmap item and measured result.
labs.expected: An inspectable feature/source/version table.
labs.failures: A downloaded document being hashed does not authenticate every claim inside it.

labs.title: Design a detector negative control
labs.goal: Test whether a detector label follows evidence or a loose identifier heuristic.
labs.inputs: Owned labeled positive/negative reference devices; minimized non-sensitive logs.
steps: Define the actual observable input.
Blind fixture labels and count errors.
Change identifiers/conditions and record false positives and missed detections.
labs.expected: A bounded confusion matrix with unobservable cases, not an assumption about nearby people.
labs.failures: A BLE name/OUI or RSSI is not a camera/operator identity or precise location.

labs.title: Test the recovery path
labs.goal: Demonstrate restoration rather than only normal startup.
labs.inputs: Owned noncritical fixture and a model-appropriate recovery mechanism.
steps: Preserve a known-good configuration/artifact.
Make a reversible noncritical change.
Restore, repeat the same functional observation and retain both receipts.
labs.expected: An actual restoration result under recorded conditions; hardware execution remains unclaimed until performed.
labs.failures: Do not rely on the overwritten image as the only recovery path or erase unknown storage.
